learnings.question: Who originated the idea that in an information-rich world, information consumes the one scarce resource it depends on: human attention?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that an information-rich world necessarily creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In one real-world personal AI content-curation system built by a software engineer, what single question does the AI ask before deciding whether a YouTube video gets included in the daily feed?
options: Does this video have more than 10,000 views?
Is this video under 10 minutes long?
Does this channel have a verified badge?
Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
learnings.learning: A described personal content engine pulls daily videos from hand-picked YouTube channels and uses AI to filter them with one tailored question, discarding anything that doesn't pass.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed in the 1880s that we forget about 80% of what we learn within a day unless we actively force ourselves to recall it, which is why re-reading notes doesn't work as well as being quizzed.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term do researchers behind the "Google Effect" paper use for the phenomenon of the brain forgetting information once it has been written down or stored digitally?
learnings.learning: The "Google Effect" paper calls the brain's tendency to immediately discard information once it's offloaded to a phone or notebook "Digital Amnesia."
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What is the main purpose of breaking a software development process into smaller, iterative cycles called Sprints, as practiced in the Scrum framework?
options: To eliminate the need for planning meetings
To increase the length of the project
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To reduce the number of team members needed
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a project into iterative Sprints specifically so teams can stay flexible and adjust course quickly, rather than committing to one long, rigid plan.

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact visualizes a Sprint's progress and shows how much work remains, helping the team track whether it's on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is the Scrum artifact that visualizes Sprint progress and remaining work, distinct from the Product Backlog (all possible features) and Sprint Backlog (the team's commitment for the Sprint).

learnings.question: According to Quran 51:56, for what purpose did Allah state He created the jinn and humankind?
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states, "I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me," framing worship as humanity's foundational purpose.

learnings.question: What Arabic term, referenced in Quran 2:30, describes humanity's role as caretakers or stewards of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Quran 2:30 introduces the concept of khalifah, describing humans as a "successive authority" placed on Earth with responsibility for stewardship of creation.

learnings.question: In a hadith recorded in Sahih Bukhari, what did the Prophet Muhammad ask rhetorically about his own habit of extensive worship, despite already being assured of forgiveness?
options: Shall I not give in charity?
Shall I not fast every day?
Shall I not be a grateful servant?
learnings.learning: In Sahih Bukhari 1130, the Prophet Muhammad responded to a question about his extensive worship by asking, "Shall I not be a grateful servant?", framing gratitude as central to worship.

learnings.question: In the PCIe power management spec, which power state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down — offering the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: PCIe's L2 state is the deepest power-saving state, analogous to a fully shut-down computer: it maximizes power savings but takes the longest to resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Within the L1 power state of PCIe, what happens as a link moves from substate L1.0 toward the deeper substates L1.1 and L1.2?
options: The device fully powers off and loses all data
More power-saving components are turned off, increasing power savings but also increasing wake-up time
Power consumption stays the same but bandwidth increases
learnings.learning: L1.1 and L1.2 power down progressively more components of the main link than L1.0, trading greater power savings for longer wake-up delays.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to the actual, unfolding occurrence of events in a person's life, as shaped by their own actions and decisions?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual unfolding of events in one's life, which can be influenced by actions and sincere dua, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal knowledge and plan.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which Quranic surah contains the verse stating that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves?
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11) states that Allah does not change a people's condition until they change what is in themselves, underscoring human responsibility alongside Allah's decree.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: A data analysis applying the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) to word frequency in the Quran found that the top 20 most frequent words account for roughly what share of the entire text?
learnings.learning: Unlike the classic 80/20 Pareto split, the top 20 most frequent words in the Quran accumulate to only about 20.83% of the total text, not 80%.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What term describes the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the diacritical marks added to Arabic text to indicate vowel sounds; a word-frequency analysis of the Quran used text without Tashkeel for simplicity and uniformity.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
